lessons.title: The New Regime Slabs: Every Rate Band Explained

children.text: You met the new regime slab table in Chapter 1. This lesson takes it apart band by band, shows you a ready reckoner that lets you compute slab tax on any income in one line, and explains what changed when the table was redrawn. By the end you should be able to work out new regime slab tax in your head faster than you can open a calculator app.

body.label: Legal Home of the New Regime
body.context: The default regime for individuals, HUFs, AOPs, BOIs and artificial juridical persons. You pay tax under it unless you actively opt for the old regime.

children.text: The new regime table follows two simple rules. Every slab is exactly ₹4,00,000 wide, and each slab's rate is 5 percentage points higher than the one below it. The staircase stops at 30%, which applies to everything above ₹24,00,000. Once you remember those two rules, you never need to look the table up again.

body.caption: New Regime Ready Reckoner, Tax Year 2026-27
headers: Cumulative Slab Tax at Top of Slab

cells: Freshers at IT services firms, junior bank staff
Mid-level government employees, 3 to 5 year professionals

children.text: The fourth column is the one to memorise: 0, 20,000, 60,000, 1.2 lakh, 2 lakh, 3 lakh. With it, any income becomes a one-step calculation. Find the threshold just below the income, take the cumulative tax at that threshold, and add the slab rate on the excess.

body.caption: X is Total Income; L means lakh. Result is slab tax before rebate, surcharge and cess

children.text: Try it on Meenakshi, a radiologist in Coimbatore with Total Income of ₹22,60,000. The threshold just below is ₹20,00,000, where cumulative tax is ₹2,00,000. The excess is ₹2,60,000, taxed at 25%, which is ₹65,000. Slab tax: ₹2,65,000. One line, no bucket table needed.

body.title: New Regime Slab Tax as Income Rises

body.text: Notice the curve gets steeper at each threshold but never jumps. That is progressive taxation in picture form: each extra lakh costs a little more tax than the one before, up to ₹30,000 per lakh once you cross ₹24 lakh, and no single rupee of extra income ever causes a sudden leap in tax on the slab table itself.

children.text: Before You Celebrate the 5% Slab: The Rebate Changes Everything Below 12 Lakh

The 5% and 10% slabs exist on paper, but for resident individuals with Total Income up to ₹12,00,000, the rebate wipes out the entire ₹60,000 of slab tax. Add the ₹75,000 standard deduction and a salaried resident with gross salary up to ₹12,75,000 pays no income tax under the new regime. The slabs still matter, though: they decide the tax the moment income crosses ₹12 lakh, and they are what a non-resident, who gets no rebate, actually pays. Chapter 3 covers the rebate in full.

children.text: What Changed From the Previous Table

The current table was introduced in the February 2025 Union Budget, effective from FY 2025-26, and carried into the Income-tax Act, 2025. The table it replaced, used for FY 2024-25, had uneven slabs and reached 30% at just ₹15 lakh.

body.caption: Slab Tax Saved by the New Table (Before Rebate and Cess)

body.text: The saving grows up to ₹24 lakh and then stays flat at ₹1,10,000. Above ₹24 lakh both tables tax every extra rupee at 30%, so all of the benefit comes from the lower slabs. A CXO on ₹1 crore and a senior manager on ₹24 lakh got exactly the same slab tax cut in rupees.

body.title: Show me the math: FY 2024-25 slab tax at ₹20 lakh

children.text: Up to ₹3 lakh: ₹0. ₹3 to ₹7 lakh at 5%: ₹20,000. ₹7 to ₹10 lakh at 10%: ₹30,000. ₹10 to ₹12 lakh at 15%: ₹30,000. ₹12 to ₹15 lakh at 20%: ₹60,000. ₹15 to ₹20 lakh at 30%: ₹1,50,000. Total: ₹2,90,000. Under the current table the same income attracts ₹2,00,000, a saving of ₹90,000.

body.title: Compute New Regime Slab Tax in Three Moves
steps: Confirm you are working with Total Income, after the standard deduction and any allowed deductions
Find the highest threshold at or below that income: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 or 24 lakh
Take the cumulative tax at that threshold: 0, 20,000, 60,000, 1,20,000, 2,00,000 or 3,00,000
Multiply the income above the threshold by the next slab's rate and add it on

body.title: Slab Tax at ₹21.5 Lakh
body.prompt: Siddharth, a senior associate at a Mumbai law firm, has Total Income of ₹21,50,000 under the new regime. What is his slab tax, before surcharge and cess?
body.explanation: The threshold below is ₹20,00,000, with cumulative tax of ₹2,00,000. The excess of ₹1,50,000 is taxed at 25%, adding ₹37,500. Slab tax is ₹2,37,500. No rebate applies because income is above ₹12 lakh.

body.title: Above the Top Threshold
body.question: Pooja, a startup founder in Bengaluru, has Total Income of ₹30,00,000 under the new regime. What is her slab tax, before surcharge and cess?
body.explanation: Cumulative tax at ₹24 lakh is ₹3,00,000. The ₹6,00,000 above that is taxed at 30%, adding ₹1,80,000. Total: ₹4,80,000, which is 16% of her income. ₹9,00,000 is the classic mistake of applying 30% to everything, and ₹5,40,000 is the slab tax at ₹32 lakh.

body.title: Remember the Staircase
body.textWithBlank: Under the new regime, cumulative slab tax at a Total Income of exactly ₹16,00,000 is ₹___.
body.explanation: ₹0 on the first 4 lakh, ₹20,000 on the next 4 lakh at 5%, ₹40,000 on the next at 10% and ₹60,000 on the next at 15%. ₹20,000 + ₹40,000 + ₹60,000 = ₹1,20,000.

body.title: Is the Non-Resident Better Off?
body.scenario: Two sisters each have Total Income of ₹11,00,000 from Indian sources in tax year 2026-27, all taxed at slab rates. Kavya lives in Chennai and is a resident. Lakshmi lives in London and is a non-resident; her income is rent from two flats in Chennai.
body.prompt: Using the new regime slabs, what tax does each sister pay before cess, and why is there a difference?
body.modelAnswer: Both sisters have the same slab tax: ₹20,000 + 10% of ₹3,00,000 = ₹50,000. Kavya is a resident with Total Income below ₹12 lakh, so the rebate removes her entire ₹50,000 and she pays nothing. Lakshmi is a non-resident and cannot claim the rebate, so she pays ₹50,000 plus 4% cess of ₹2,000, a total of ₹52,000. The slab table is identical for both; the difference comes from the rebate, which is only for residents.

points: The new regime is the default under section 202 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 and applies unless you opt out
Every slab is 4 lakh wide and each rate is 5 points higher, from nil up to ₹4 lakh to 30% above ₹24 lakh
Memorise cumulative tax at each threshold: 0, 20,000, 60,000, 1.2 lakh, 2 lakh and 3 lakh
Slab tax at any income = cumulative tax at the threshold below + slab rate × the excess
Residents with Total Income up to ₹12 lakh pay no tax thanks to the rebate, but non-residents pay full slab tax
Compared with FY 2024-25, the current table saves up to ₹1,10,000 of slab tax, with the maximum reached at ₹24 lakh

body.text: Slab rates shown are for individuals under the new regime for tax year 2026-27 and, for comparison, FY 2024-25. Rates can change in each Union Budget. Figures exclude surcharge and the 4% health and education cess unless stated. This lesson is for education only and is not tax advice.
